entries.title: Matthew 26:2
segments: The Son of man is delivered up. An emphatic prediction of the betrayal found only in Matthew.

entries.title: Matthew 26:3
segments:
Then were gathered together. Probably an informal gathering of the great council, the Sanhedrin.
 

 
The court of the high priest. The central quadrangle around which the palace was built.
 

 
Caiaphas. Joseph Caiaphas, son-in-law of Annas.  He was appointed high priest in A.D. 26 by the Roman procurator Valerius Gratus.

entries.title: Matthew 26:6
segments: Simon the leper. Simon's disease must have been cured, otherwise he would not have been allowed to have guests in his house.

entries.title: Matthew 26:7
segments: A woman having an alabaster cruse. Mary, the sister of Lazarus (

).  The cruse was a vase with a long neck.
 

 
Exceeding precious. The ointment was worth about $150.

entries.title: Matthew 26:12
segments: To prepare me for burial. Another prediction of his death.

entries.title: Matthew 26:13
segments: That also which this woman hath done. Mary's act won higher praise from Jesus than any other mentioned in the New Testament.  It was a most touching proof of devotion, and a sign of recognition of Christ's true nature and work.  The anointing has had a place in the Christian consciousness ever since and will have unto the end of time.

entries.title: Matthew 26:15
segments: Willing to give. The motive was greed.  See

entries.title: Matthew 26:17
segments: On the first day of unleavened bread. The Feast of Unleavened Bread began on the 14th of Nisan, the first month of the Jewish year, in the evening, that is, in the beginning of the 15th day.  It was popularly identified with the Passover.

entries.title: Matthew 26:18
segments:
Such a man. Probably a disciple who had been informed and who was ready and willing to do what was required of him.
 

 
My time is at hand. The time of his betrayal and crucifixion.

entries.title: Matthew 26:24
segments: Good were it for that man, etc.  An expression often used among the Jews in condemnation of one who knew the law, and did not obey it.

entries.title: Matthew 26:25
segments: Thou hast said. A common form of assent in Palestine.

entries.title: Matthew 26:26
segments: And as they were eating, Jesus took the bread. The institution of the Last Supper is recorded in
.  See
.  It was on the 14th, which began after sunset on the 13th of Nisan.  In

the words 'I keep the Passover at thy house' may be taken as spoken by our Lord with the intention of following the ritual of the Passover as far as possible.  That would be according to his declaration that he came to fulfill the law; but on the other hand he was instituting a new rite to be observed by his followers for all time, so that the Passover ritual would, if necessary, be modified.  Some think there was no paschal lamb, Christ himself being offered as a sacrifice, doing away forever with the necessity of the typical lamb without blemish.

entries.title: Matthew 26:28
segments:
This is my blood. The wine poured from the cup was a symbol of the blood shed for the remission of sins.
 

 
For many. Mankind.

entries.title: Matthew 26:30
segments: When they had sung a hymn. The second part of the Hallel (
).  'Hallel' meaning praise, was a term of the Hebrew religious service applied to certain psalms, especially to those above indicated.

entries.title: Matthew 26:32
segments: I will go before you into Galilee. That is, I will lead you as a shepherd into Galilee.  Jesus after again predicting his resurrection, continues in these words the figure of a shepherd going before his flock, in harmony with Zechariah's prophecy quoted in
.  The disciples were to meet in Galilee.  See

entries.title: Matthew 26:33
segments: But Peter answered. Impulsive arrogance here characterized the words of Peter as on former occasions.  He declared in effect that his loyalty and affection for his Master were deeper than those of the other apostles.

entries.title: Matthew 26:34
segments: Before the cock crow. Before dawn.  Mark says: Before the cock crow twice (
).  The two expressions practically mean the same, as the cock crows at frequent intervals in the early morning.

entries.title: Matthew 26:35
segments: Even if I must die with thee, etc.  Peter's sinful presumption and audacity increased even after Jesus warned him.  Hence the humiliation of his denial was correspondingly deep.

entries.title: Matthew 26:36
segments: Gethsemane. Literally, 'the oil press'.  It was at the foot of the western slope of the Mount of Olives, and was probably an olive yard.  Like all the other gardens of Jerusalem, it was outside the city walls.

entries.title: Matthew 26:37
segments: Peter and the two sons of Zebedee. Peter, James and John were closest to Jesus and were better fitted than the others to witness his agony in the garden.  They had been with him on the Mount of Transfiguration.

entries.title: Matthew 26:39
segments: Not as I will. The human nature of our Lord sought deliverance from his coming trial, yet he submitted to the will of his Father.

entries.title: Matthew 26:40
segments: Saith unto Peter. As Peter was first in professing loyalty so he first received the rebuke of Jesus for failure to act according to his profession.

entries.title: Matthew 26:44
segments: A third time, saying again the same words. A proof of his intense earnestness and anguish.  Contrast this with the 'vain repetitions' of

entries.title: Matthew 26:46
segments: Let us be going. To meet those who were coming to take him.  It was impossible that the disciples should sleep on.  The sudden appearance of Judas and those with him prevented it.

entries.title: Matthew 26:47
segments: A great multitude. It was composed of part of the Jewish Temple guard (
), a detachment of Roman soldiers (
), servants of the high priest (

) and probably some of the more bigoted among the elders and chief priests.  The size of the crowd indicated that the power of Jesus was feared.  It was necessary for the Jews to make the Roman governor believe that they were arresting a dangerous political agitator.

entries.title: Matthew 26:48
segments: Whomsoever I shall kiss. The kiss, thus debased by Judas to a sign of treachery, was sometimes given by a pupil to a master but more often by a master to a pupil.  In addressing our Lord as Rabbi, or Master, Judas showed that he intended to avail himself of this custom.

entries.title: Matthew 26:50
segments: Friend. The Greek word stands for an expression of civility rather than for friendliness.  It was a word often used in reply by a rabbi to a pupil.

entries.title: Matthew 26:51
segments: One of them. Peter.  See

.
 

 
The servant. Malchus (

entries.title: Matthew 26:52
segments: All they that take the sword, etc.  In his most perilous hour Jesus fearlessly affirmed in effect that warfare in his behalf must be carried on by the power of the Spirit.

entries.title: Matthew 26:53
segments: Twelve legions of angels. Our Lord could have invoked almighty power to save himself, but obediently fulfilled his Father's will as revealed in the Scriptures.

entries.title: Matthew 26:58
segments:
Peter followed him afar off. He was evidently the first of the disciples to recover from the terror caused by the arrest of Jesus.
 

 
Unto the court of the high priest. Outside the room into which Jesus was taken for examination.

entries.title: Matthew 26:59
segments: Sought false witness against Jesus. It was illegal for judges to seek any witness, but to seek a false witness was infamous.  Both the spirit and the letter of Jewish law were ignored in the proceedings before the Sanhedrin.  Murder was in the hearts of its members.

entries.title: Matthew 26:61
segments: I am able to destroy, etc.  These witnesses did not report the words of our Lord correctly.  See

entries.title: Matthew 26:63
segments: Tell us whether thou art the Christ, the Son of God. The attempt to obtain an answer from Jesus having failed through the latter's silence, the high priest asked him the most searching and decisive question that was possible, an affirmative answer to which made any further proof unnecessary.

entries.title: Matthew 26:64
segments: Thou hast said. See note on

entries.title: Matthew 26:65
segments: Rent his garments. This was according to custom, on proof of a charge of blasphemy.  It would have been contrary to the hostile intention of the high priest or of the Sanhedrin to take any honest step towards investigating the claim of Jesus to be the Christ, the Messiah.

entries.title: Matthew 26:66
segments: He is worthy of death. This condemnation was illegal because passed on the same day as the trial.  Jewish law required a delay of one day in such cases.  The trial itself was informal, and it was also illegal because held at night on the eve of the Passover feast.

entries.title: Matthew 26:68
segments: Prophesy. At this moment Jesus was blindfolded (

entries.title: Matthew 26:70
segments: He denied before them all. See

.  The denials of Peter that are recorded by the other three evangelists do not differ from these in essential points.  There are only variations of minor detail, such as would appear in the accounts of witnesses who were intent upon the main issue and the most striking scenes, and therefore not careful about those of less importance.

entries.title: Matthew 26:71
segments: Into the porch. The entrance hall from the street.  Beyond this was the court or quadrangle, open to the sky, and around which were built the different rooms of the house of the high priest.

entries.title: Matthew 26:73
segments: Thy speech maketh thee known. Peter's Galilean dialect.

entries.title: Matthew 26:75
segments: Peter remembered. See

.
 

 
He went out, and wept bitterly. Out from the porch or entrance passage into the street.  Repentance and remorse drove him away from the throng.
